name: aws configure
description: Interactively set access keys, default region, and output format for a profile.

flags.description: Configure a named profile instead of default
Show the current resolved configuration and where each value came from
Read or write a single config value
flags.example: aws configure set region eu-west-1 --profile staging

examples.description: Check which credentials and region are in effect

examples.command: aws configure set region us-east-1 --profile dev

examples.description: Print the resolved temporary credentials as export statements (for tools that only read env vars)

notes: Writes to ~/.aws/credentials and ~/.aws/config. Prefer `aws login` (console credentials), IAM Identity Center (`aws configure sso`) or role credentials over long-lived access keys.
`aws configure mfa-login` creates a profile with temporary credentials from an IAM user plus an MFA code.

name: aws configure sso
description: Create a profile that authenticates through IAM Identity Center (AWS SSO).

examples.description: Interactive wizard: start URL, region, account, and role
Create a reusable sso-session block shared by several profiles

notes: Results in a profile in ~/.aws/config that uses short-lived credentials refreshed by `aws sso login`.

name: aws sso login
description: Sign in through IAM Identity Center and cache temporary credentials.

flags.description: Log in to a named sso-session
Use the device code flow (e.g. on a remote/headless machine)
Use a fixed localhost port for the browser callback (instead of a random one)

examples.description: Open the browser to authenticate the dev profile

notes: Uses the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE by default; pass --use-device-code where the browser callback cannot reach the CLI.
For IAM users, root or federated console users without IAM Identity Center, use `aws login` instead.

name: aws login
description: Sign in to the CLI with your AWS Management Console credentials and get auto-refreshing temporary credentials.

flags.description: Profile to sign in to (created if it does not exist)
Cross-device flow for SSH/headless hosts: open the URL elsewhere and paste the authorization code
Fixed localhost port for the browser callback

examples.description: Open the browser, pick a console session and configure the default profile
Sign in to (or create) a named profile
Sign in from a machine without a browser
Delete cached login credentials for all profiles (or use --profile for one)

notes: Requires AWS CLI 2.32.0 or later and the SignInLocalDevelopmentAccess managed policy on the IAM user/role (root needs none).
Works for root, IAM users and federated console sign-ins; for IAM Identity Center use aws configure sso / aws sso login.
Writes login_session = <arn> to the profile in ~/.aws/config and caches tokens under ~/.aws/login/cache. Credentials refresh automatically for up to the session duration (maximum 12 hours).

name: aws sts get-caller-identity
description: Show the account, user/role ARN, and user ID of the current credentials.

examples.description: Check who you are authenticated as

notes: Works with any valid credentials and needs no IAM permissions: the first thing to run when debugging auth.

name: aws sts assume-role
description: Get temporary credentials for an IAM role, e.g. in another account.

flags.description: ARN of the role to assume
Identifier for the session (shows up in CloudTrail)
MFA device ARN and current code if the role requires MFA

examples.description: Assume a role and print temporary credentials

examples.command: aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/Deploy --role-session-name me --query Credentials --output json

notes: Usually easier: add `role_arn` and `source_profile` to a profile in ~/.aws/config and use --profile; the CLI assumes and refreshes the role automatically.

name: --profile / --region / --output / --query
description: Global options that work with every AWS CLI command to pick credentials, region, and format output.

flags.description: Use a named profile (or set AWS_PROFILE)
Output format: json, text, table, yaml, yaml-stream, or off (suppress output)
JMESPath expression to filter output client-side
Check permissions without making the change (EC2 and some other services)
Error output style: enhanced (default), json, yaml, text, table, or legacy

examples.description: Set defaults for the shell session
Readable table of instance IDs and states

notes: --query filters after download; use service-side --filter/--filters options to reduce data on large accounts.
Most commands auto-paginate; use --max-items and --starting-token to page manually.

name: aws update
description: Update the AWS CLI v2 to the latest version.

examples.description: Download and install the latest AWS CLI version

notes: Only works for installs made with the official installer, install script, or aws update itself; use brew, your package manager, or a new container image otherwise.
The downloaded install script is signature-verified; --skip-signature-verification disables that check and is not recommended.

name: aws s3 ls
description: List buckets, or objects and prefixes within a bucket.

flags.description: List all objects under the prefix
Print total object count and size
Only list buckets whose names start with this prefix
Only list buckets located in this region

name: aws s3 cp
description: Copy files between local disk and S3, or between S3 locations.

flags.description: Filter files by pattern (evaluated in order)
Canned ACL such as bucket-owner-full-control (ignored/rejected on buckets with ACLs disabled, the default since 2023)
Skip objects that already exist at the destination
Tag uploaded objects; repeat as --tags key value (local to S3 only)
Checksum to calculate on upload, e.g. CRC32, CRC64NVME, SHA256

examples.command: aws s3 cp report.csv s3://<bucket-name>/reports/ --no-overwrite --tags team platform
examples.description: Upload only if the key does not exist yet, and tag the object

notes: Since early 2025 the CLI calculates CRC checksums by default on uploads and no longer sends Content-MD5; some S3-compatible (non-AWS) services need request_checksum_calculation = when_required in ~/.aws/config.

name: aws s3 sync
description: Sync a directory and an S3 prefix, copying only new or changed files.

flags.description: Delete destination files that do not exist in the source
Show what would happen without doing it
Compare by size only, ignoring timestamps
Only upload/download files missing at the destination

examples.description: Deploy a static site, removing stale files

notes: WARNING: --delete removes objects in the destination; run with --dryrun first (and enable bucket versioning for important data).

name: aws s3 mv
description: Move or rename objects (copy then delete the source).

name: aws s3 rm
description: Delete objects from S3.

flags.description: Delete all objects under a prefix

examples.description: Delete all objects and then the bucket

notes: WARNING: Deletion is permanent unless bucket versioning is enabled. `aws s3 rb --force` deletes the bucket and everything in it.

name: aws s3 mb
description: Create a new S3 bucket.

flags.description: Region to create the bucket in
Tag the new bucket; repeat as --tags key value

examples.description: Create a bucket in a specific region

examples.command: aws s3 mb s3://my-app-assets-123456 --tags team platform --tags env prod

notes: Bucket names are globally unique, lowercase, 3-63 characters. New buckets block public access, disable ACLs (bucket owner enforced) and use SSE-S3 encryption by default.

name: aws s3 presign
description: Generate a temporary pre-signed URL to download an object without credentials.
notes: URLs signed with temporary (SSO/role) credentials expire when those credentials expire, even if --expires-in is longer.

name: aws s3api
description: Low-level S3 API calls for bucket settings and object metadata not covered by aws s3.

examples.description: Get object metadata (size, ETag, content type)

examples.command: aws s3api get-bucket-policy --bucket <bucket-name> --query Policy --output text | jq .

name: aws ec2 describe-instances
description: List EC2 instances and their details.

examples.description: Table of running instances with names and IPs
Find instance IDs by Name tag

notes: Instances are nested under Reservations; the `Reservations[].Instances[]` pattern flattens them.

name: aws ec2 start-instances / stop-instances
description: Start, stop, or reboot EC2 instances.

flags.description: Hibernate instead of stop (if enabled on the instance)
Force stop without a graceful OS shutdown

examples.description: Block until the instance is running

notes: Stopping loses instance-store data and changes the public IP unless an Elastic IP is attached.
WARNING: `aws ec2 terminate-instances` permanently deletes instances; there is no undo.

name: aws ec2-instance-connect ssh
description: SSH to an EC2 instance with a one-time key pushed through EC2 Instance Connect, optionally via an Instance Connect Endpoint for private subnets.

flags.description: direct, eice (via EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint) or auto (default)

examples.description: SSH to an instance without managing key pairs
Reach an instance in a private subnet through an Instance Connect Endpoint
Open a local tunnel to the instance's SSH port for other tools

notes: Requires a local OpenSSH client and the EC2 Instance Connect package on the instance (preinstalled on Amazon Linux and Ubuntu AMIs).
AWS recommends setting --connection-type explicitly because the auto behavior may change.

name: aws iam list-users
description: List IAM users in the account.

examples.description: Table of users and creation dates
Show managed policies attached to a user

name: aws iam create-user
description: Create a new IAM user.

examples.description: Create access keys for the user (shown only once)

notes: Prefer IAM Identity Center for humans and IAM roles (e.g. OIDC for CI) for workloads instead of long-lived user keys.

name: aws iam attach-user-policy
description: Attach a managed policy to an IAM user.
notes: Attaching policies to groups or roles scales better than per-user policies.

name: aws lambda list-functions
description: List Lambda functions in the region.

name: aws lambda invoke
description: Invoke a Lambda function and save the response to a file.

flags.description: Send --payload as raw JSON (required in CLI v2 for plain JSON)
Return the last 4 KB of logs, base64 encoded

examples.command: aws lambda invoke --function-name my-function --cli-binary-format raw-in-base64-out --payload '{"id": 42}' response.json && cat response.json
examples.description: Invoke synchronously with a JSON payload

examples.command: aws lambda invoke --function-name my-function --invocation-type Event --cli-binary-format raw-in-base64-out --payload file://event.json /dev/null

notes: The outfile argument is required. A 200 StatusCode with FunctionError set still means the function threw.

name: aws lambda update-function-code
description: Deploy new code to an existing Lambda function.

flags.description: Publish a new version after updating

examples.command: zip -r function.zip . && aws lambda update-function-code --function-name my-function --zip-file fileb://function.zip

notes: Use fileb:// (binary) for zip files, not file://.

name: aws logs tail
description: Stream or read recent CloudWatch Logs from a log group.

examples.description: Interactive Live Tail session (takes log group ARNs; can tail several groups at once)

name: aws ecr get-login-password
description: Get an ECR auth token and log Docker in to a private registry.

examples.command: aws ecr get-login-password --region us-east-1 | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com

examples.description: Tags of the most recently pushed image

notes: Token is valid for 12 hours. `aws ecr get-login` (v1) was removed; use get-login-password.

name: aws cloudformation deploy
description: Create or update a CloudFormation stack from a template via a change set.

flags.description: Create the change set but do not run it (review first)
Exit 0 when there is nothing to change (CI friendly)

examples.command: aws cloudformation deploy --template-file template.yaml --stack-name my-app --parameter-overrides Env=prod --capabilities CAPABILITY_IAM

notes: WARNING: `aws cloudformation delete-stack` deletes every resource in the stack unless it has a Retain deletion policy.

name: aws ssm start-session
description: Open a shell or port forward to an instance through Systems Manager, no SSH or open ports needed.

examples.description: Tunnel to a private RDS database via the instance

notes: Requires the Session Manager plugin installed locally and the SSM agent + instance profile on the target.

name: aws secretsmanager get-secret-value
description: Retrieve the value of a secret from Secrets Manager.

examples.command: aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id prod/my-app/db --query SecretString --output text
aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id prod/my-app/db --query SecretString --output text | jq -r .password
examples.description: Extract one field from a JSON secret
Read a Parameter Store value instead

notes: Avoid printing secrets in CI logs or shell history.

description: Read items from a DynamoDB table.

flags.description: Primary key in DynamoDB JSON for get-item
Limit results returned by the CLI

examples.description: Get a single item by key
